question: Can a reflection be perceived without directly perceiving the original?
premises: A reflected form may be grasped even when the original is not directly grasped.
One can see in a mirror the body of a beloved person standing behind oneself.
The mirror example supports the same possibility for auditory reflection.
inference: Perception of a reflection does not require direct perception of the original.
uncertainties: paśyeṭṭaṅkitaṃ is read as paśyet ṭaṅkitam with the transmitted sandhi.
plain_english: A reflection can be perceived even without perceiving the original directly, just as one may see in a mirror the body of a beloved person standing behind oneself.
